title: Color Picker Selection crosshair fails to appear after several hours of runtime

judgment.rationale: Use the existing fix URL and validate its exact build coverage rather than proposing a competing broad lifecycle rewrite. The source change addresses the concrete invalid-desktop-handle failure evidenced by this archive, but the report's hours-later symptom is not proven fully resolved or shipped in the author's installed binary. Treat a remaining failure on a build containing the guard as a distinct follow-up with activation/process state, not grounds to discard the supplied stack.
evidence: The author reports intermittent missing selection UI after hours of runtime, with other modules working and a PowerToys restart restoring Color Picker.

The supplied 0.101.2362 report contains WPF/MEF composition failure constructing MouseInfoProvider; its root message is 'Controlador no válido' (invalid handle). This is more specific than an unproven generic long-running event-loop leak.
Current main has a TryGetPixelColor guard for Win32Exception/ExternalException during construction and sampling, introduced with merged #49174, and no longer uses the old MEF composition path.

Source inspected at main 9227a8497750: src/modules/colorPicker/ColorPickerUI/Mouse/MouseInfoProvider.cs: Both constructor and update sampling use TryGetPixelColor; invalid-handle/GDI failures return false instead of throwing through object construction. https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/9227a8497750c257a0682b53c556d07f48ed8ff3/src/modules/colorPicker/ColorPickerUI/Mouse/MouseInfoProvider.cs

Source inspected at main 9227a8497750: src/modules/colorPicker/ColorPickerUI/Helpers/NativeEventWaiter.cs: Current activation uses a captured DispatcherQueue and named-event worker; this differs from the WPF assembly in the report. https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/9227a8497750c257a0682b53c556d07f48ed8ff3/src/modules/colorPicker/ColorPickerUI/Helpers/NativeEventWaiter.cs

Source inspected at main 9227a8497750: src/modules/colorPicker/ColorPickerUI/Helpers/AppStateHandler.cs: Session/overlay visibility is a separate state boundary to inspect if a guarded current build still fails to show. https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/9227a8497750c257a0682b53c556d07f48ed8ff3/src/modules/colorPicker/ColorPickerUI/Helpers/AppStateHandler.cs
Downloaded the report and read the full October 20–21 Color Picker stack. Inspected #49174's merged commit patch for the exact guard; no full uptime run or installed-version coverage was claimed.
judgment.recommended_action: Validate the existing invalid-handle guard before a lifecycle rewrite

reproduce.title: Validate the existing invalid-handle guard before a lifecycle rewrite
reproduce.version_requirement: A signed/test build confirmed to contain merged #49174, compared with the supplied 0.101.2362 WPF stack.
prerequisites: Use an isolated test account or controlled test machine; preserve existing user data.
steps: 1. Verify the actual loaded Color Picker binary/UI implementation rather than assume a PowerToys version alone contains the guard.
2. On a controlled account, exercise startup and activation around lock/unlock or a disconnected/reconnected desktop, then return to an interactive desktop.
3. Confirm transient pixel-capture failure does not terminate construction/process and that subsequent sampling recovers.

4. Run an uptime/activation control; if the UI is still absent, distinguish process exit, undelivered activation and stale overlay-visible state while preserving the original stack as a separate matched signature.
reproduce.expected_result: The known invalid-handle branch is non-fatal and sampling recovers; any residual hours-later activation defect is recorded with its own first failure rather than a duplicate patch.
